Privacy policy

Effective date: November 12, 2026

This is the privacy policy of MyVibe, the Android app. MyVibe ("the app") is published by DeeperWork. It writes draft replies in your own voice for the chats you choose. This policy explains what the app reads, what it keeps on your phone, what leaves your phone and when, what our service stores, and how to delete it. Questions or requests: nick@deeperwork.ai.

The short version

  • MyVibe reads the conversation on your screen only in the chat apps you turn on in Settings, Chat apps, and only while one of them is in front, after you agree to the in-app disclosure and turn on its Accessibility service yourself. Instagram and Google Messages are turned on when you tap Agree on the app's first screen, which also turns on ongoing learning (described below) and shows both disclosures; every other app stays off until you turn it on, and Android sends MyVibe nothing from an app that is off. You can turn any of them, and learning, off in Settings.
  • With MyVibe Pro (including its free trial), when a new message arrives in a one-to-one Instagram or Google Messages chat that is not open, MyVibe also reads that app's notification (the sender's name and the messages shown) and, for a chat it read on your screen before, drafts your reply right away, so it is ready in the message box when you open the chat. MyVibe only reads those notifications: it never taps, replies from, or dismisses one. You can turn this off in Settings, Draft new messages before you open them.
  • On the Instagram inbox, and at the top of a one-to-one Instagram chat you open, it also reads the names and handles shown and keeps them on your phone, so it can tell people apart.
  • MyVibe never taps, scrolls, sends, or accepts anything in those apps. The only thing it does there is set the text of the message box: when you tap Insert or Clear the message box, and, with Insert drafts automatically on (the default, in Settings), on its own when a draft is ready and the box is empty. It does not replace text you typed, unless all you typed is a word such as "Message" that some apps show in an empty box. A draft that holds a link, email address, phone number or @handle the conversation does not already contain, or repeats six or more words in a row from your notes about the person or your voice profile, is never put in on its own: it waits in MyVibe's sheet for you to check. You decide whether to use a draft and press Send yourself.
  • To write a draft, the conversation on your screen and your notes go to the MyVibe service, which asks an AI model for the draft and returns it. By default this happens automatically when you open a one-to-one chat where the other person wrote last, also for people who are not in your People yet and for texts in Google Messages (never for message requests, group chats, or chats where MyVibe cannot tell who wrote what); you can turn Auto drafts off. The service does not store your messages, your drafts, your profile, or your people.
  • Your imported messages, your profile, and your notes stay on your phone, encrypted. To build your profile, your own messages (some with the message they answered) are sent after the app automatically replaces names, handles, numbers, emails, addresses, and links with placeholders. That replacement is automatic, not guaranteed (details below), and the service stores none of it.
  • No ads, and no analytics or tracking SDK of our own. The Google Play version includes Google's Play Billing Library, which can send its own diagnostics to Google (details below). We never sell or share your data for advertising.

What the app reads on your phone

  • The chat on your screen (Accessibility). With your consent, the app's Accessibility service reads the conversation that is on screen while one of the chat apps you turned on is in front. You choose the apps in Settings, Chat apps: Instagram and Google Messages are turned on when you agree on the app's first screen, and every other messaging app is off until you turn it on, after a screen that says what MyVibe will do there. The service tells Android to send it events from those apps only, so it receives nothing from any other app, and, apart from the notifications described below, it reads nothing while any other app is in front. Apps other than Instagram and Google Messages are read best effort; when MyVibe cannot tell who wrote what, it drafts only when you ask. In every app, a message that looks like a one-time code (a word such as code, PIN or verification with a number of 4 to 8 digits) is replaced by "[one-time code]" before anything uses the reading, so it is never saved or sent. In text message apps (Google Messages, Samsung Messages, Textra), a chat with a short code (3 to 6 digits, such as a bank or a delivery service) is not read at all, and a chat whose sender shows as a short name in capitals (such as a bank's alert name) is drafted only when you ask. You can turn an app off in Settings, Chat apps, or the whole service off in Android Settings under Accessibility. Your consent is tied to the text of the disclosure you accepted (the first-run screen or the accessibility disclosure): if an update changes what that text says MyVibe reads, does or sends, MyVibe reads nothing until you accept the new text (Settings shows "Reading is paused"). An update that only rewords the text, or changes only which chat apps a new install turns on, can keep your earlier consent.
  • Notifications of Instagram and Google Messages (Accessibility, MyVibe Pro). While you have accepted the disclosure and Settings, Draft new messages before you open them (on by default), Auto drafts and the Toggle Drafting switch are all on, Android also hands the same service the notifications that the chat apps you turned on in Settings, Chat apps show when they alert you, whatever your plan. MyVibe uses only those of Instagram and Google Messages, and only with MyVibe Pro (including its free trial); without MyVibe Pro, and for every other chat app, it makes no draft from them and sends nothing. From such a notification it reads only the conversation part: the sender's name, the messages shown and their times, your own account's name in that app, the chat's title, and whether it is a group. It never reads or uses the notification's buttons, its reply input or what happens when you tap it, and it never taps, replies from, dismisses, or posts a notification. It uses the notification only when it belongs to a one-to-one chat that MyVibe read on your screen earlier while the service was running; notifications for group chats, message requests, a chat it cannot tie to exactly one person, another account signed in to the same app, short codes and automated senders, and your own messages are skipped. The new messages are joined, in the phone's memory only, with the conversation MyVibe read on your screen, to write the draft described under "What leaves your phone". While your phone is locked, Android gives MyVibe only a hidden version of most chat notifications, so a message that arrives then usually gets no early draft; nor does one that arrives silently (silent mode, Do Not Disturb). With any of those switches off, Android hands MyVibe no notifications at all.
  • The Instagram inbox and chat header (Accessibility). When the inbox list is on screen, the same service reads the display name and handle of each chat listed, and when you open a one-to-one Instagram chat it reads the name and handle shown at the top; it keeps them on your phone (up to 3,000 entries), so it can match a name to a handle later. It does not open any chat. These names and handles are not sent anywhere on their own; a person's name or handle leaves the phone only with a draft for that person (below).
  • Your name in a chat app. Some apps (for example Discord or LinkedIn) show a name above every message. To tell your messages from the other person's, MyVibe keeps your own name in that app on your phone: the one you type in Settings, Chat apps, or the author name it sees on your own message right after a draft is inserted (by you or automatically) and you send it (it compares only the length of that message with the draft, and keeps no text). It is not sent on its own.
  • Which chat apps are installed. To list your messaging apps in Settings, Chat apps, the app asks Android whether each app on its list of known messaging apps is installed, and which apps can receive shared text (for Add another app). It cannot see any other app, and it sends nothing about your apps anywhere.
  • Files and text you choose to import. To learn how you write, you can import your own message history: an Instagram or Facebook data export, a WhatsApp chat export shared to the app, a Telegram Desktop export (the machine-readable JSON file), a text backup file made by SMS Backup & Restore, text you paste into the app, or text you share to MyVibe from another app (shared text is imported like pasted text). The app reads only the files and text you give it, through Android's file picker, the share sheet, or the paste box, and needs no storage permission. Get my Instagram messages opens Meta's Download your information page, and Get my texts opens SMS Backup & Restore (or its Google Play page); you request or save the file there yourself, MyVibe does nothing in that app or page and learns nothing from it, and it reads the file only when you choose it. When another app shares a chat export or text with MyVibe, nothing is imported until you tap Import it on MyVibe's import screen; when several shares are waiting, MyVibe says how many and names each file first. Discard drops them and keeps nothing from them, and Delete everything and Delete imported history drop any that are still waiting. Exports contain both sides of your chats: the app keeps the other person's messages on your phone as the context of your replies (see "What leaves your phone").
  • Texts on the phone (sideloaded version only). The version installed outside Google Play can offer to read the text messages stored on the phone once, to learn your voice, only after its own disclosure and your consent. It reads both the texts you sent and the texts you received (with the other person's number) and keeps them on your phone with your imported history. The Google Play version never reads text messages; it imports a backup file instead.
  • What you type into the app: notes about a person, corrections to your profile, custom instructions, and, in the sideloaded version, your own Anthropic API key if you choose to use one.

What is stored on your phone

  • Your imported messages, both yours and the ones you received (to build your profile), your profile, your people (labels, notes, summaries, the style learned for each, and the names and handles read from the Instagram inbox and chat headers), your settings (including which chat apps are on and your name in each), and, if you turn on ongoing learning, your own messages in Instagram or Google Messages (the ones you send, and your earlier ones that are visible on screen in the chats you open, also when you scroll up) and the differences between drafts and what you sent there. Ongoing learning follows only those two apps, and only while they are turned on in Settings, Chat apps; it never stores the other person's messages.
  • All of it is in the app's private storage, which other apps cannot read. Your messages, profile, people, and learning records are in a database encrypted with a key kept in the Android Keystore. The install token, your own API key (if any), and the random salt the app uses to make thread keys are also encrypted with the Android Keystore. Your settings and choices (which chat apps are on, Auto drafts, Insert drafts automatically, Draft new messages before you open them, Toggle Drafting, your name in each chat app, which notices you accepted, and the bubble's position) are kept in the app's private preferences, which are not encrypted.
  • Some things are kept only in the app's memory while its Accessibility service runs, never written to storage: the recent conversation of the chats MyVibe read on your screen (up to 100 chats) and drafts written when a new message arrived (up to 30, each for at most 3 hours and only on the same day). A draft written on arrival is not shown, used or learned from until you open that chat and it matches the chat on screen. Both are cleared when you turn drafting off, when you use Delete everything, when you turn the chat app off, or when the service stops.
  • Nothing is included in Android backups or device-to-device transfers.
  • Files you export yourself. Only when you tap them, two actions write a file outside the app's own storage: Settings, Export my profile writes your profile (including examples of your own messages) as a file where you choose; Diagnostics, Dump this screen writes the structure of the last screen MyVibe read, with every text replaced by placeholder letters (it keeps the layout and word lengths), and opens the share sheet. Neither file leaves the phone unless you send it somewhere yourself.

What leaves your phone, and when

All traffic goes over HTTPS (encrypted in transit). The app talks only to the MyVibe service, plus Google Play for subscriptions in the Google Play version (including the Play Billing Library's own diagnostics, under "Who processes it").

  1. When you ask for a draft, or when the app drafts automatically: automatic drafts are on by default. When you open a one-to-one chat where the other person wrote last, the app sends the request below without a tap, whether or not the person is in your People (for texts in Google Messages too). Message requests and group chats are never drafted automatically (you can still ask for a draft), and you can turn Auto drafts off in Settings, or turn all drafting off with the Toggle Drafting switch at the bottom of the sheet (then nothing is sent for a draft). The request holds: the conversation on your screen (up to the last 40 messages, with each sender's name in a group chat), the name or handle shown in the chat, what you keep for that person (label, relationship type, notes, summary, the style learned for them, when you last talked, and whether they are new), your own name and your profile, your drafting preferences (length target, punctuation choices), the time and your time zone, the app version, and, when you regenerate, earlier unused drafts and your own edit. When you regenerate and the new draft is too close to one you passed over, the service may ask the AI once more within the same request, with that draft added to the earlier unused drafts; it still counts as one draft. The service uses this to write the draft and does not store it. With MyVibe Pro (including its free trial), the same request is also sent when a new message arrives in a one-to-one Instagram or Google Messages chat MyVibe read on your screen before, with the new messages taken from that app's notification (above), so the draft is ready when you open the chat. The request then also says that it was made on arrival. Such a draft is written, and counts as a draft, even if you never open the chat. Turn it off in Settings, Draft new messages before you open them.
  2. When you build or update your profile: your own messages from the sources you imported, some with the message they answered for context (up to 300 characters, which can be a text or message you received); if you turn on ongoing learning, your own messages MyVibe saw in Instagram or Google Messages after you turned it on (including your earlier ones visible on screen in the chats you opened) and your edited drafts, as context (if you have no profile yet, your first profile is built from those messages once MyVibe has seen about 30 of them); and, for the people you write to most, a small batch of your recent messages to each, to learn how you write to that person. Each message goes with its time, how long you took to reply, the chat app, whether it was a group, and the kind of relationship (friend, family, client, and so on). Every batch carries your own name, unmasked, so the profile can refer to you. The app also sends statistics about your writing (lengths, rates, counts, and words that many of your conversations share), your profile corrections and custom instructions, and the previous profile when it updates one. Before anything is sent, the app automatically replaces names, handles, phone numbers, email addresses, street addresses, and links with placeholders. The replacement is designed to over-mask rather than miss: when it is unsure whether a word is a name, it masks it. It is automatic, though, and it can still miss something, such as an unusual name or contact detail written in an unusual way, so we do not claim it catches everything. The service uses what it receives only to write your profile, returns observations and the profile, and never stores the messages or the profile. The observations it derives from a batch (statements about your writing with message IDs, never message text) may be held in the service's memory for up to 24 hours, so a retried batch is not processed twice; they are never written to its database.
  3. When the app registers or checks in: a random install ID made by the app (not linked to your Google account or device identifiers), the SHA-256 fingerprint of the app's signing certificate, the app version, whether it is the Google Play or sideloaded version, and your time zone (so daily limits count your days). Nothing else about your device is sent, apart from the Google Play integrity token in the Google Play version once its integrity check is turned on (under "Who processes it").
  4. When you subscribe or restore a purchase (Google Play version): the Google Play purchase record (product, base plan, purchase token, and Google's signed receipt), so the service can verify it with Google Play. Payment itself is handled by Google Play; we never see your card or payment details. When the service is set up to check subscriptions with Google Play directly, it also asks Google Play for your subscription's current state and receives Google Play's notices when it changes (for example a renewal, a cancellation or a refund). These name only the purchase, which the service matches by the hash it keeps; nothing new about you is stored.
  5. When you open Plan: a request for your usage numbers (drafts today and this month, free drafts used).
  6. Your own Anthropic key (sideloaded version only, optional): sent with each draft request in a request header (x-byo-key). The service uses it for that one request and never stores or logs it.
  7. To make drafts faster: when you open a chat app you turned on, or when a draft is about to be written, the app may send a short request with no content, no install ID and no token, at most once a minute, so the service is ready; it carries nothing about you or your chats. Every request also names the service's region (a fixed value, us-west-2), so it runs next to the service's database.

The "Manage subscription in Google Play" button opens play.google.com in your browser or the Play Store app. The "Privacy policy" link on the Welcome screen opens this policy at https://deeperwork.github.io/myvibe/privacy/ in your browser; the app sends nothing to that page. "Get my Instagram messages" opens Meta's Download your information page at accountscenter.instagram.com in the Instagram app or your browser, and "Get my texts" opens SMS Backup & Restore or its page on play.google.com; the app sends nothing to those pages.

Reporting a draft. Under a draft in the sheet, "Report this draft" opens your own email app with a new email to nick@deeperwork.ai. It holds a line asking what is wrong, the text of that draft as MyVibe wrote it (without your edits), and the app version. MyVibe adds nothing else: not the conversation, names, handles, your notes, or your profile. The draft's own words go in as written, though, and a draft can greet the person by first name or refer to something from the chat, so read it and delete anything you do not want to send. You can change or delete any of it before sending, and nothing is sent unless you send it yourself from your email app; MyVibe never sends it. If you send it, we receive only what you left in the email, from your email address, and use it only to look into the report and improve the drafts. We keep it no longer than 12 months (under "How long we keep it"); ask us at the same address to delete it sooner.

Who processes it

  • The MyVibe service (operated by DeeperWork, hosted on Supabase at a supabase.co address) receives the requests above.
  • Supabase (our hosting provider) keeps its own platform logs of the requests that reach the service: for example the time, the address path, the status, and network details such as your IP address, country, and user agent. They hold no message content. Supabase keeps these logs for the retention period of our hosting plan (1 day on the Free plan, 7 days on Pro, 28 days on Team), and we use them only to run and secure the service.
  • Anthropic (the provider of the Claude AI model) receives, from the service and not from the app, the content of a draft or profile request so the model can write the draft or the profile. Anthropic processes it as our service provider under its commercial terms for API customers, and does not train its models on it. Under those terms Anthropic deletes API inputs and outputs within 30 days, unless it must keep them longer to enforce its usage policy (flagged content up to 2 years) or by law. The service also uses Anthropic's prompt caching, which holds parts of a request (such as your profile) in Anthropic's cache for up to an hour so a following request is faster and cheaper. With your own key (sideloaded version), the request is made under your Anthropic account and its terms.
  • Google Play handles subscriptions and payments. The Google Play Billing Library inside the Google Play version includes Google's own logging components (Google's data transport), which can send diagnostics about the library itself (such as errors and timings of billing calls) to Google under Google's privacy policy. We do not receive or control that data, and it holds no message content. The library also brings Google Play services code, including a location module, but the app declares no location permission, so it cannot read your location. Once we turn on Google Play's integrity check, the Google Play version, when it registers and with each paid request (your plan, drafts, and profile building), asks Google Play for an integrity token (Google's encrypted verdict on whether the app is the genuine one from Google Play and the device passes Google's checks), which the MyVibe service sends to Google's Play Integrity service to check that the request comes from the genuine app; the service keeps only the pass or fail result and when it was checked (the last integrity verdict, under "What the MyVibe service stores"), never the token or the full verdict. The sideloaded version never asks for one.

We do not sell your data, share it with advertisers or data brokers, or use it for advertising.

What the MyVibe service stores

  • Install record: the random install ID, a SHA-256 hash of the install token (never the token), the signing certificate fingerprint, the distribution (Google Play or sideloaded), the app version, the time zone it registered with (so daily limits count your days), when it was created and last seen, abuse flags, and the result of the last integrity check (passed or failed) and when it was checked.
  • Plan: the plan state, its source, the product and base plan, a SHA-256 hash of the purchase token (never the token or the receipt), its expiry, and when it was last checked.
  • Complimentary access: only for installs we give free use to by hand (such as our own test phones): the install ID, a short label such as "owner", when it was granted, when it ends, and its own daily draft limit, if it has one. Nothing else. Each grant or removal is also written to our admin change log with only the first 8 characters of the install ID, the label, the end date and the daily draft limit; that log is kept as a record of our own changes.
  • Daily counters: drafts, profile batches, full profile builds, AI tokens used, and the estimated cost, per day. Drafts written on arrival are also counted on a second counter of the same install, so they never use up the free drafts. The service also keeps service-wide daily totals of AI use and estimated cost, one of them for free use, that are not linked to any install or network address.
  • Rate limits: counters for the current one-minute window only, keyed by a hash of the install token or by a keyed hash of the network address made with a random value that the service holds only in memory and replaces every day (never the address itself, and the random value is never stored).
  • Service logs: one line per request with the route, a shortened hash of the install ID, the status, the duration and how it split between the service and the AI model, whether a draft was asked for on screen or on arrival, the error code, and sometimes a fixed cause code (for example that the app integrity check could not run). No message text, names, or content.

The service never stores message text, drafts, your profile, your people or notes, names, handles, phone numbers, email addresses, purchase receipts, tokens, API keys, or network addresses in its database or its own logs. The hosting provider's platform logs are described under "Who processes it".

How long we keep it

  • On your phone: until you delete it (below) or uninstall the app.
  • On the MyVibe service: the install record, plan, complimentary access, and daily counters are kept while the install is in use, and are deleted when you use Delete everything in the app, when you ask us, or automatically once the install has not contacted the service for 13 months (395 days), unless it then has an active subscription (including a trial or grace period) or complimentary access. Counters left behind by a request that finished after its install was deleted are removed within a day. Rate-limit counters only ever cover the current minute and are removed within a minute after it ends. The service-wide daily totals, which identify no install or network address, are kept. Draft and profile requests are not kept at all; observations derived from a profile batch may stay in the service's memory for up to 24 hours.
  • At our hosting provider: platform request logs for the retention period of our Supabase plan (1 to 28 days).
  • At Anthropic: API inputs and outputs are deleted within 30 days under its commercial terms, with the exceptions above.
  • Draft reports you email us ("Reporting a draft"): kept in our mailbox only as long as we need to look into the report, and no longer than 12 months after it arrives, or deleted sooner when you ask.

Deleting your data

  • In the app: Settings, Privacy, Delete everything wipes everything MyVibe stores on the phone and deletes the install's records on the MyVibe service (install record, plan, counters). It also clears the clipboard if it still holds a draft MyVibe copied there (a draft MyVibe copies is marked sensitive, so Android 13 and later hide it in the clipboard preview); anything else on the clipboard is left alone. When it is done, MyVibe tells you whether the service confirmed. If the service cannot be reached, MyVibe keeps only this install's key and asks the service again to forget the install each time MyVibe starts, until the service confirms. If MyVibe cannot read the install's key (or you delete from the screen MyVibe shows when its storage cannot be opened), the service cannot be told: its records of that install stay until the automatic deletion after 13 months without contact, which waits while a subscription or complimentary access is in force (under "How long we keep it"). One thing stays on the phone: in the Google Play version, the Google Play Billing Library's own diagnostics queue (Google's data transport, described under "Who processes it"), which holds no message content and is removed when you uninstall. Settings, Voice, Delete imported history wipes the imported messages and keeps your profile and people.
  • Uninstalling removes everything on the phone. The service's install record stays until it is deleted automatically after 13 months without contact (not while a subscription or complimentary access is still in force; cancel a subscription in Google Play), or until you ask us (or use Delete everything before uninstalling).
  • By email: write to nick@deeperwork.ai from any address with the request; we delete the records we can match to your request within 30 days. The service does not know who you are, so the reliable way to delete its records is Delete everything in the app, before you uninstall.
  • A Google Play subscription is cancelled in Google Play, not in the app.

Permissions the app uses

  • android.permission.INTERNET: to reach the MyVibe service.
  • android.permission.ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE: added by Android libraries to check for a connection before a request.
  • android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS: optional notifications while an import or profile build runs, and one reminder about a day after you tap Get my Instagram messages, to check whether Meta's file is ready.
  • android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE and android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC: so an import or profile build can keep running when you leave the app.
  • com.android.vending.BILLING: subscriptions through Google Play (Google Play version only).
  • android.permission.READ_SMS: the sideloaded version only, never the Google Play version. If you choose "Read my texts directly" and agree to its notice, MyVibe reads the texts stored on your phone once to learn how you write. It reads the texts you sent and the texts you received and keeps them on your phone with your imported history. Your own texts are used to learn your voice; a received text is used only as the message one of your replies answered, and some are sent with that reply when your profile is built. Names, handles, numbers, emails, addresses, and links are replaced with placeholders on the phone before anything leaves it (automatically, so it can miss something), and MyVibe never sends texts.
  • <applicationId>.DYNAMIC_RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED_PERMISSION: an internal, signature-level permission AndroidX adds so only the app itself can reach its own internal receivers. It grants no access to your data.
  • The Accessibility service is protected by android.permission.BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE, which only Android itself holds; you turn the service on in Android Settings.

Children

MyVibe is not directed to children and is not meant for anyone under 18. We do not knowingly collect data from children. If you believe a child has used the app, contact us and we will delete the install's records.

Security

HTTPS only (the release app refuses unencrypted connections), encrypted storage on the phone, no backups, hashed identifiers on the service, and no message content stored on the service. No method is perfectly secure; tell us at the address below if you find a problem.

Changes

If this policy changes, the new version is posted at the same address with a new effective date.
